summary: Utils/core-misc test coverage is broad and high quality (align-1 IR-contract tests, refcount ladders, vector growth/edge cases, cross-process cache survival, fingerprint via compile_kernel). The material defects are doc/API drift in the pysqlite_bridge writeup (a documented RTLD_GLOBAL import-preload side effect that does not exist, and a Py_DEBUG 'not supported' claim the code contradicts) plus utils.rst omitting automodule sections for four public modules (clock, meminfo, standard, void_type). Lesser gaps: Any.reset old-payload release is not refcount-asserted, and timer.py / get_str_from_p_as_int edge values are untested.

findings.title: pysqlite_bridge docs claim a non-existent RTLD_GLOBAL import-preload side effect
findings.claim: The 'Import order matters on macOS' note states: 'Importing numbox.utils.pysqlite_bridge preloads Python's libsqlite3 with RTLD_GLOBAL so subsequent numba JIT compiles resolve sqlite3 symbols to the same library. Import this module before anything that touches numbox.core.bindings._sqlite_*.' No such preload exists in the module. A user who follows this guidance (importing the bridge first to fix macOS symbol resolution) gets no symbol-resolution effect and may ship a broken macOS setup believing the import handled it. The actual macOS fix is the add_symbol path in the module docstring's 'macOS caveat' section, which is a different mechanism entirely.
findings.evidence: pysqlite_bridge.py imports only 'import ctypes', 'import sqlite3', and 'from numbox.core.bindings._sqlite_conn import sqlite3_errmsg, sqlite3_libversion' (lines 35-38); grep for RTLD_GLOBAL / preload / load_library / CDLL in the module returns nothing. There is no module-level CDLL(..., mode=RTLD_GLOBAL) call. The module's own docstring (lines 7-33) describes the correct mechanism (read addresses from _sqlite3.so and register via add_symbol) which contradicts the RST's RTLD_GLOBAL-preload claim.
findings.recommendation: Delete or rewrite the 'Import order matters on macOS' paragraph in docs/numbox.utils.rst (210-217) to match the module docstring's actual add_symbol mechanism, or remove the import-order instruction if no import side effect performs symbol coordination.

findings.title: Doc says Py_DEBUG builds are unsupported, but pysqlite_bridge code explicitly supports them
findings.claim: utils.rst states 'Assumes a release Python build; Py_DEBUG builds shift the sqlite3 *db field by 16 bytes for refcount tracing and are not supported.' The code DOES support debug builds: _pyobject_head_fields() detects them via sys.gettotalrefcount and prepends the two extra _ob_next/_ob_prev pointers so the db offset is correct. The doc therefore misrepresents a supported configuration as unsupported, which could cause a debug-build user to avoid a working path (or a maintainer to delete the working detection believing it dead).
findings.evidence: pysqlite_bridge.py lines 52-56: 'if hasattr(sys, "gettotalrefcount"): fields += [("_ob_next", ctypes.c_void_p), ("_ob_prev", ctypes.c_void_p),]' -- exactly the 16-byte (two pointers) debug shift the doc says is unsupported. The _PysqliteConnection docstring (lines 80-88) confirms 'the layout is correct across 32/64-bit, debug, and free-threaded builds.'
findings.recommendation: Update docs/numbox.utils.rst lines 219-221 to state debug builds ARE handled (via gettotalrefcount detection), or if intentionally unsupported, remove the gettotalrefcount branch. Add a test asserting _pyobject_head_fields() includes _ob_next/_ob_prev under a simulated debug build to pin the behavior the doc currently denies.

findings.title: utils.rst omits automodule for four public modules (clock, meminfo, standard, void_type)
findings.claim: The sphinx page for numbox.utils has automodule directives only for highlevel, preprocessing, digest, fingerprint, lowlevel, cstrings, pysqlite_bridge, timer. It omits clock.py (public @intrinsic monotonic_ns), meminfo.py (public bridge intrinsics export_meminfo/borrow_structref/release_meminfo/structref_meminfo/get_nrt_refcount), standard.py (make_params_strings), and void_type.py. clock and meminfo are non-trivial public API; their absence from docs is real API/doc drift -- consumers (numbduck/numbarrow) reading the rendered docs won't see these documented.
findings.evidence: grep 'automodule' docs/numbox.utils.rst yields 8 directives (highlevel, preprocessing, digest, fingerprint, lowlevel, cstrings, pysqlite_bridge, timer). On-disk numbox/utils has additional non-underscore modules clock.py, meminfo.py, standard.py, void_type.py with public symbols (e.g. clock.py defines 'monotonic_ns' as an @intrinsic; meminfo.py defines export_meminfo/borrow_structref/release_meminfo/structref_meminfo/get_nrt_refcount).
findings.recommendation: Add '.. automodule:: numbox.utils.clock' and '.. automodule:: numbox.utils.meminfo' sections (and standard / void_type if they are part of the public surface) to docs/numbox.utils.rst, mirroring the existing automodule blocks.

findings.title: Any.reset old-payload release is not refcount-asserted (a leak/double-free on overwrite would pass)
findings.claim: ol_reset overwrites self.p (the ErasedType holding the previous _Content) on every reset. Correctness depends on numba's structref setattr decref'ing the old field value exactly once. test_10 calls any.reset(...) three times but never asserts the refcount of the PREVIOUSLY-held content is decremented after a reset. A regression where reset leaks the old content (no decref) or double-frees it (extra decref) would not be caught: the test only checks the NEW value reads back and that the new content's refcount rises to 2. The risky path (releasing the old payload) is exercised but its refcount balance is unverified.
findings.evidence: any_type.py ol_reset (lines 59-66): 'self.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType); self.t = ty_code' -- overwrites self.p without an explicit decref, relying on setattr semantics. test_any_type.py test_10 asserts get_nrt_refcount(s1)==2 after any.reset(s1) (new content incref) but performs no get_nrt_refcount check on the string/float content held before that reset, nor after the final any.reset(11). Contrast test_5, which does a full incref/decref ladder for make_any but not for reset.
findings.recommendation: Extend test_10 (or add a test) to bind a structref, reset Any onto it, capture get_nrt_refcount, then reset Any onto a different value and assert the first structref's refcount dropped by exactly 1 (old-payload released once -- neither leaked nor double-freed).

findings.title: get_str_from_p_as_int only tested on one non-empty ASCII string; empty-string and multibyte edges untested
findings.claim: get_str_from_p_as_int builds the result with 'chr(char_as_code_p)' per byte and exits on the first NUL. The only direct test passes one ASCII string. Two edges are unexercised: (a) an empty C string (first byte NUL) should return '' -- untested; (b) the per-byte chr() means a multibyte UTF-8 sequence is decoded byte-by-byte as Latin-1-like codepoints, so a non-ASCII C string round-trips WRONG -- there is no test pinning that boundary (the cstrings UTF-8 round-trip test uses the separate ctypes helper str_from_p_as_int in auxiliary_utils, not this @njit function). The empty-string case in particular is a trivial-to-add regression guard.
findings.evidence: lowlevel.py get_str_from_p_as_int (lines 249-260): 's += chr(char_as_code_p)' in a loop that 'return s' on the first zero byte. test_lowlevel.py test_get_str_from_p_as_int builds 'a random string' (ASCII) only. test/auxiliary_utils.py str_from_p_as_int (lines 59-67) is a distinct ctypes BytesIO+utf-8 decoder used by the cstrings UTF-8 test -- it does not exercise the numbox @njit function.
findings.recommendation: Add an empty-string case (c_char_p(b'') -> get_str_from_p_as_int returns '') to test_lowlevel.py, and an explicit assertion documenting the ASCII-only contract for the @njit reader (or a COR follow-up if multibyte support is intended).

findings.title: timer.py (Timer decorator) has no unit test
findings.claim: numbox/utils/timer.py defines a Timer decorator that records per-function durations into a class-level Timer.times dict and logs at WARNING. No test imports numbox.utils.timer for assertion -- only stress/benchmark scripts (not collected by pytest as unit tests) use timing. The class-level mutable 'times = {}' shared across all Timer instances is a design hazard (cross-instance/cross-test state bleed) with no test guarding it. Low severity (diagnostic-only utility) but it is a public module with zero coverage.
findings.evidence: grep for 'numbox.utils.timer' / 'from numbox.utils import timer' in test/ returns only test/stress_work.py, test/benchmark_work.py, test/stress_work_runner.py -- none are pytest-collected unit tests asserting Timer behavior. timer.py line 10: 'times = {}' is a class attribute shared by every Timer instance.
findings.recommendation: Add a small test/utils/test_timer.py exercising Timer()(func) records into Timer.times keyed by __name__ and returns the wrapped result; optionally pin/​document the shared class-level times dict.

findings.title: digest's _Unfingerprintable fallback for a real (non-codeless) FunctionType is untested
findings.claim: digest() has a branch (lines 44-52) where a genuine FunctionType whose _fingerprint_function raises _Unfingerprintable or RecursionError falls back to cloudpickle of __code__. test_digest covers the deterministic path, the codeless-callable path (partial), and jit-option/subject variation, but never a function that IS a FunctionType yet is un-fingerprintable (e.g. one closing over an un-canonicalizable value). The except clause is exercised only indirectly via compile_kernel's _formula_fingerprint tests, not through digest() itself, so a regression that broke digest's fallback (e.g. swallowing the wrong exception) could pass digest's own suite.
findings.evidence: digest.py lines 44-52: 'if isinstance(py, FunctionType): try: h.update(_fingerprint_function(py, set())...); continue; except (_Unfingerprintable, RecursionError): pass' then cloudpickle fallback. test_digest.py tests cover cb (fingerprintable), functools.partial (codeless), and empty inputs -- none constructs a FunctionType that triggers the _Unfingerprintable except branch inside digest.
findings.recommendation: Add a test_digest case passing a closure over an un-canonicalizable value (e.g. a lambda capturing an object with no canonical form) and assert digest() returns a 16-char hash (fallback succeeds) rather than raising.
